technicalCollocations.meaning: The most demanding or computationally intensive part of a task or architecture.
technicalCollocations.example: The backend GPU cluster handles the heavy lifting of 3D geometry processing.
technicalCollocations.notes: Commonly used in engineering discussions to describe load distribution.

technicalCollocations.meaning: A specific stage where data flow, processing, or execution slows down.
technicalCollocations.example: A severe CPU bottleneck occurs when thousands of individual draw calls are dispatched without batching.
technicalCollocations.notes: Always paired with prepositions like 'at' or 'in'.

technicalCollocations.meaning: To find an acceptable compromise between two competing constraints.
technicalCollocations.example: We need to strike a balance between high visual fidelity and mobile WebGL frame rates.
technicalCollocations.notes: Idiomatic alternative to 'find a middle point'.

technicalCollocations.meaning: To make a process or pipeline more efficient and less complex.
technicalCollocations.example: Our custom Blender export script streamlines the asset preparation workflow significantly.
technicalCollocations.notes: Frequently used in performance reviews and resumes.

technicalCollocations.meaning: The automated compiler or bundler process of stripping out unused functions and modules.
technicalCollocations.example: Tree shaking performs dead code elimination to minimize final client bundle size.

technicalCollocations.meaning: Very detailed, precise, and low-level control over a system or setting.
technicalCollocations.example: The compute shader gives us granular control over every individual vertex position.

technicalCollocations.meaning: Combining software modules or libraries with no friction or noticeable transitions.
technicalCollocations.example: The WebGL canvas provides seamless integration within our React application shell.

technicalCollocations.meaning: A framework, library, or pattern proven reliable under heavy real-world production stress.
technicalCollocations.example: Zustand is a battle-tested state management solution for complex client applications.

technicalCollocations.meaning: Features that function immediately upon installation without requiring custom configuration.
technicalCollocations.example: Unity delivers out-of-the-box support for glTF binary asset importing.

technicalCollocations.meaning: The ability of a system to maintain core functions when some components fail or hardware is limited.
technicalCollocations.example: The 3D viewer implements graceful degradation, falling back to static 2D images if WebGL is disabled.
technicalCollocations.notes: Core principle in resilient web and game engineering.

technicalCollocations.meaning: A component whose individual failure will stop the entire system from functioning.
technicalCollocations.example: Relying on a single centralized authentication server creates a dangerous single point of failure.

technicalCollocations.meaning: The implied future cost of rework caused by choosing an easy, short-term solution over a better approach.
technicalCollocations.example: Hardcoding asset paths allowed a fast demo but accumulated severe technical debt.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To investigate, examine, or analyze specific details of a problem.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: Let's drill down into the profiler timeline to identify which script is allocating memory.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To add more details, substance, or structure to a basic concept or proposal.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: We have the core architecture drafted; now we need to flesh out the error handling edge cases.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To resolve minor discrepancies, bugs, or differences smoothly.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: We still need to iron out a few browser rendering glitches before the release tomorrow.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To increase the pace, capacity, volume, or learning speed.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: It took the new frontend engineer about one sprint to fully ramp up on our codebase.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To gradually discontinue, replace, or retire a legacy system or feature.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: We are phasing out WebGL 1.0 support in favor of modern WebGL 2.0 pipelines.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To resist, question, or negotiate against an unrealistic request or timeline.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: Alex had to push back on the Friday deployment deadline due to unresolved QA tickets.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To return to a topic or person at a later time.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: Let's table this discussion for now and circle back to it after reviewing the telemetry data.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To make brief contact with someone to check status or exchange quick updates.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: I will touch base with the lead designer this afternoon regarding the button color tokens.

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To guide someone step-by-step through a document, codebase, or UI flow.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: Could you walk me through the shader graph node setup for the cross-section plane?

workplacePhrasalVerbs.meaning: To direct all attention and focus precisely on a specific target or root cause.
workplacePhrasalVerbs.example: The team zeroed in on the memory leak after running automated stress tests overnight.

formalVsInformalPairs.context: We will commence the performance audit (formal) vs Let's kick off the sprint (informal).
Terminate the idle background process (formal) vs Kill the frozen process (informal).
We must investigate the root cause (formal) vs I'll look into it (informal).
The engineering team resolved the concurrency defect (formal) vs We fixed the bug (informal).
We leverage GPU compute capabilities (formal) vs We use the GPU (informal).
Subsequent API iterations will support streaming (formal) vs In the next version... (informal).
We can expedite the security patch review (formal) vs Let's speed up the review (informal).
This implementation is technically feasible within budget (formal) vs That sounds doable (informal).
To mitigate latency spikes, we enabled caching (formal) vs To cut down delay... (informal).
We will collaborate with the infrastructure team (formal) vs Let's team up (informal).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: Real, existing in fact, current reality (e.g. 'The actual performance was 60 FPS').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'actual / del momento presente'. Para 'actual' en español, usa 'Current' o 'Present'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: Current build version (versión actual) vs Actual execution time (tiempo de ejecución real).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: In the end, after a period of time or delay (e.g. 'The promise will eventually resolve').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'eventualmente / de vez en cuando'. Para 'a veces/ocasionalmente', usa 'Occasionally' o 'Sometimes'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: It will eventually succeed (con el tiempo / al final tendrá éxito).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: A collection of pre-compiled routines or modules (e.g. 'Standard library').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: En español se traduce como 'biblioteca de software/código', NO 'librería' (que en inglés es 'bookstore').
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: Import the React library (importar la biblioteca React).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: A trade-off / mutual concession OR to endanger/weaken security (e.g. 'Security was compromised').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'compromiso' como obligación moral o deber. Para 'compromiso/deber', usa 'Commitment' o 'Obligation'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: We reached a compromise (llegamos a un acuerdo/concesión) vs Our team commitment (nuestro compromiso de equipo).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: To become aware of something or understand clearly (e.g. 'I realized the shader was missing').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'realizar / ejecutar una tarea'. Para 'realizar/llevar a cabo', usa 'Perform', 'Execute', o 'Carry out'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: I realized the bug existed (me di cuenta del error) vs Execute the test (realizar la prueba).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: To continue after an interruption (e.g. 'Resume playback') OR a curriculum vitae.
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'resumir'. Para 'hacer un resumen', usa 'Summarize' o 'Wrap up'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: Resume the download (reanudar la descarga) vs Summarize the findings (resumir los hallazgos).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: Reasonable, practical, showing good judgment (e.g. 'A sensible architecture choice').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'sensible / emotivo / delicado'. Para 'sensible', usa 'Sensitive'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: A sensible decision (una decisión sensata/razonable) vs Sensitive user data (datos sensibles del usuario).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: To help or support someone (e.g. 'The AI assistant assists developers').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'asistir a una reunión / evento'. Para 'asistir a un evento', usa 'Attend'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: Assist with debugging (ayudar con la depuración) vs Attend the standup meeting (asistir a la reunión).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: To behave as if something is true when it is not / to feign (e.g. 'Do not pretend it works').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'pretender / tener la intención de'. Para 'pretender/intentar', usa 'Intend', 'Aim', o 'Attempt'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: We intend to ship on Friday (pretendemos lanzar el viernes) vs Pretend mock data (fingir datos de prueba).

falseFriendsTechESEN.trueEnglishMeaning: Big in size, extent, or capacity (e.g. 'A large dataset').
falseFriendsTechESEN.falseSpanishCognate: NO significa 'largo' en dimensión lineal/tiempo. Para 'largo', usa 'Long'.
falseFriendsTechESEN.correctUsage: A large file (un archivo grande) vs A long cable / long meeting (un cable largo / reunión larga).
